page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance type within the general purpose N2 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, allocating exactly 1.0 GB of memory per core. The hardware configuration includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. No dedicated GPUs or local storage devices are included in this profile, requiring workloads to rely on external network-attached block volumes.

Benchmark results place the multi-core capabilities and system throughput solidly in the average performance tier, achieving 29778.72 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9659.0. Conversely, single-thread throughput exhibits lower comparative performance, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 1150.0 and a single-core stress-ng score of 1409.48, both falling in the bottom 25% category. Memory performance shows high uncached write bandwidth at 91.03 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%, while uncached read bandwidth reaches 177.33 GB/sec. Additionally, the instance shows strong text generation capabilities on lightweight small language models, recording 284.06 tokens per second.

With a 1:1 ratio between vCPU count and RAM capacity, the instance optimizes resource allocation for high-concurrency CPU tasks that do not require heavy in-memory data sets. It maintains cost efficiency by eliminating excess RAM overhead for CPU-heavy pipelines, though the lack of bundled local disks and weak single-threaded performance are architectural tradeoffs to consider. The n2-highcpu-32 is appropriate for multi-threaded compilation, batch data transformation, static web serving, and distributed CI/CD worker pools.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-32 is a compute-skewed virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It lacks integrated GPUs and local storage, relying on external network storage options. Performance benchmarks position the instance within the average tier for multi-core throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 9659.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 28275.53. However, single-core execution is weak, marked by a 1150.0 Geekbench single-core score. Uncached write memory bandwidth is strong at 91.03 GB/sec. Eliminating surplus memory improves resource density for compute-bound scenarios, making the instance well matched for parallel code compilation, CI/CD runners, batch encoding, and static web serving.
